offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The alert looks transient and tied to the whole-stack recreation at 01:43:19. Every container, including ledger-consumer (started 01:43:26) and Kafka, was recreated. Provider webhooks queued up during the restart and the ledger consumer fell behind by about 250 messages. It then drained the backlog: its posted rate climbed from 0.24/s to 3.4/s between 01:43 and 01:48. By 01:48 lag was 0 on every partition for both consumer groups. I found no persistent fault. I did not observe the 250-message lag itself, because my lag metric only covers the last few minutes and shows 0. The restart cause is an inference from timing, not something I confirmed in logs.

evidence.shows: Summed consumer lag is 0 at every point from 01:43 to 01:48, so the alert's symptom (250 behind) is not present now.
Per-partition lag is 0 for the ledger and payment-confirmer groups on all 3 partitions at 01:44, 01:46 and 01:48. Samples exist only from 01:44 because the receiver restarted.

The ledger consumer's posted rate ramps from 0.24/s to 3.37/s between 01:43 and 01:48, with a small already_processed rate (idempotent skips of redelivered events). Payment-confirmer shows the same drain pattern. This is consistent with a backlog being worked off. No error outcomes appear.
All services were recreated at 01:43:19 on the same image with the idempotent ledger handler and dead_letter bad-event handling. This is a stack-wide restart, not a change to one service.
All services are running and healthy with 0 restarts. Ledger-consumer started at 01:43:26 and payment-confirmer at 01:43:27.

The money check passed on all five invariants: 1102 provider events each posted exactly once, ledger balanced, and ledger, payments and refunds all agree with the provider. So the lag caused no lost, duplicated or mismatched money.

proposed_fix.summary: No fix is needed now: lag has cleared and the books reconcile. Keep watching consumer lag for a few minutes to confirm it stays near 0. If the alert fires again without a restart, look at ledger-consumer logs and traces for slow handlers. Consider raising the alert's duration or threshold so a short restart backlog does not page. A rollback would not help, because nothing was deployed or changed in behavior.
